warnings: The public AIM Defence brand spans Australian, Canadian and UK entities, but reviewed filings do not establish the legal parent-subsidiary chain or which entity holds Fractl IP, contracts and Canadian staff.

Australia's AIM DEFENCE business-name registration ended August 9, 2026 while the website remained active; current Canadian AIM Defence Inc. is corporation 1782284-7 and the former Canadian namesake is now AIM Kernel Inc.

Public Fractl labels and specifications vary by date and configuration: Fractl:1, Tactical, Civil, less than 100 versus less than 120 kilograms, and demonstrated or reported engagement ranges from 500 metres to 1.5 kilometres.

The 2024 Canadian and Australian trials support bounded prototype performance; they do not establish universal range, weather performance, certified swarm defeat, formal acceptance, operational fielding or combat use.

AIM's operationally proven and sold-on-three-continents language is not supported by disclosed customer names, quantities, acceptance dates or operational-use records in the reviewed sources.
